title_en: From Quarterback to CIO: John McArthur on Alts, AI, and the Future of Wealth at Krilogy
title_zh: 从四分卫到 CIO：Krilogy 的 John McArthur 谈另类投资、AI 与财富管理的未来
subtitle_zh: Krilogy 首席投资官 John McArthur 聊从大学四分卫到 CIO、60-20-20 配置与 AI 冲击。
description: From Quarterback to CIO: John McArthur on Alts, AI, and the Future of Wealth at Krilogy

turns.en: Welcome to The Derivative by RCM Alternatives. Send it. Hello there. Welcome back to The Derivative brought to you by RCM Alternatives where yours truly just won the annual golf outing last week.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 RCM Alternatives 出品的 The Derivative。Send it。大家好，欢迎回到由 RCM Alternatives 带来的 The Derivative，你们的主持人本人上周刚赢下公司的年度高尔夫球赛。

turns.en: All my team had Jeff Eisenberg, Colm Oz from Ohio, and Jamie from Arkansas, rounding out the winning team. Speaking of golf, we're doing a few golf events in and around the President's Cup, which is coming to Chicago to Medina this month.
turns.zh: 我们夺冠队里有来自 Ohio 的 Jeff Eisenberg 和 Colm Oz，还有来自 Arkansas 的 Jamie。说到高尔夫，这个月 Presidents Cup 要来 Chicago 的 Medina 球场，我们也会在前后办几场高尔夫活动。

turns.en: So go check it out. Let us know if you can make some of the events at rcmolts.com slash golf. Okay, on to this episode where I sit down with John McArthur, CIO of Crilogy Financial, who we first started talking with five plus years ago and has really been looking into alts in a big way since then, and are now nearly at $6 billion under management.
turns.zh: 大家去看看吧，如果能来参加其中一些活动，在 rcmalts.com/golf 上告诉我们一声。好，进入本期节目：我和 Krilogy Financial 的 CIO John McArthur 坐下来聊。我们最早开始接触是五年多前，从那以后他们真的大举研究另类投资（alts），如今管理规模已接近 60 亿美元。

turns.en: Impressive. We'll forgive them for being Cardinals fans during the Cubs postseason run here, but how do they view the market? How do they use alts?
turns.zh: 很了不起。虽然他们是 Cardinals 球迷，在 Cubs 打季后赛这段时间我们姑且原谅他们。那他们怎么看现在的市场？他们怎么用另类投资（alts）？

turns.en: And what should I do with my college savings? Send it. All right, everyone, we're here with John McArthur. How are you, John? I'm great, Jeff.
turns.zh: 还有我该拿我的大学教育储蓄怎么办？Send it。好的各位，我们今天请到了 John McArthur。John，你好吗？我很好，Jeff。

turns.en: Pleasure to be on. Thanks for having an easy name for me to pronounce. Sometimes there's five minutes of me figuring out how to pronounce the guest's name, but you're right on it.
turns.zh: 很高兴上节目。谢谢你的名字这么好念。有时候我得花上五分钟琢磨嘉宾的名字怎么发音，你这个一下就念对了。

turns.en: We're here. What are we recording on? End of August, I think tomorrow, it's a Friday. Tomorrow's week zero of college football, and we were just chatting offline for a second.
turns.zh: 我们这是在录节目。今天是哪天来着？八月底，我记得明天是周五。明天是大学橄榄球的 week zero（第 0 周），我们刚才在场外聊了一会儿。

turns.en: You got some college football experience? A little bit. Yeah, a little bit of college football experience. A long time ago, I was at Mizzou for a couple years.
turns.zh: 你有过大学橄榄球的经历？有一点。是啊，有一点点大学橄榄球经历。很久以前，我在 Mizzou 待了两年。

turns.en: University of Missouri, and then Northwestern for a couple of years. So had a unique experience to get a couple of years at both places. And you don't look like an interior delineman.
turns.zh: 就是 University of Missouri，然后又去了 Northwestern 两年。所以两所学校各待了两年，这段经历挺特别的。而且你看上去不像内线锋线球员（interior lineman）。

turns.en: What were you playing? I'm not an interior delineman. I was a quarterback. Nice. Yeah. A little backup, some backup action and special teams.
turns.zh: 你打什么位置？我可不是内线锋线球员，我是四分卫（quarterback）。不错啊。是啊，主要打替补，替补上场一些，还打特勤组（special teams）。

turns.en: So there you go. So what, high school star in Missouri and then ended up at Mizzou? Yep, ended up at Mizzou. Missed most of my senior year, actually.
turns.zh: 就这样。那你是在 Missouri 读高中的球星，然后进了 Mizzou？对，最后去了 Mizzou。其实我高中最后一年大部分比赛都没打上。

turns.en: I broke my foot a week before. In high school? Yeah, a week before game one. Missed most of my senior year, unfortunately, but that's how those things go.
turns.zh: 我在赛季开始前一周脚骨折了。高中的时候？对，第一场比赛前一周。很遗憾错过了高中最后一年的大部分比赛，但这种事就是这样。

turns.en: Did they win the state title without you? We did not win the state title. We wouldn't have won it with me or without. So fun, fun, fun experience.
turns.zh: 没有你他们拿到州冠军了吗？我们没拿到州冠军。有我没我都拿不到。总之是一段很有趣的经历。

turns.en: So let's do a little, was Missouri was in the big 12 when you were there? It was, yeah. That dates. Yeah. Now SEC, so what do you have, a big 12 preview or an SEC preview or just a Missouri preview?
turns.zh: 那我们聊两句，你在 Missouri 的时候他们还在 Big 12 吧？对，在 Big 12。这暴露年龄了。是啊。现在进 SEC 了，那你是要来个 Big 12 前瞻，还是 SEC 前瞻，或者只聊聊 Missouri？

turns.en: Yeah, gosh. Or none of the above. Yeah. Probably none of the above as I'm still, you know, I'm involved to some extent, pay attention a little bit, but not nearly as I did at one point in time.
turns.zh: 天呐。或者以上都不是。对。大概是以上都不是，我多少还参与一些、还关注一点，但远不如当年那么投入了。

turns.en: Mizzou should be good. I've looked forward to going to a couple of games this year. I was surprised. When they joined the SEC, I didn't feel like they would be able to hang and they've done a pretty good job of.
turns.zh: Mizzou 今年应该不错，我还挺期待今年去看几场比赛。他们刚加入 SEC 的时候我很意外，我原以为他们撑不住，结果他们做得相当好。

turns.en: They did. Yeah, they hung right away. Yeah, they've done a good job. And then I'm going to sneak some bears fandom in here. That Luther Burton, who came from Mizzou is just unbelievable.
turns.zh: 确实。是啊，他们立刻就站稳了，干得不错。然后我要偷偷夹带一点 Bears 球迷的私货：从 Mizzou 出来的 Luther Burden 简直不可思议。

turns.en: We're excited about what he can do. Incredible. Yeah. It should be a big year for him. Let's hope so. Stay healthy. Now come with. Incredibly.
turns.zh: 我们很期待他能有怎样的表现。太厉害了。是啊，今年对他来说应该是大年。希望如此，保持健康。现在来看，真的是不可思议。

turns.en: That's for sure. Do you ever sit here now and curse like you could have gotten all this NIL money and all that, all that stuff? It's a different era.
turns.zh: 那是肯定的。你会不会现在坐在这儿懊恼，想着当年要是有这些 NIL（姓名、形象与肖像权）的钱该多好？那是另一个时代了。

turns.en: Yeah. It's a different era. I mean, I don't know. Yeah, I don't go to that mental space, but yeah, it's fascinating how things have evolved.
turns.zh: 对，那是另一个时代。我也不知道怎么说。是啊，我不会往那个方向想，但这些年变化之大确实很有意思。

turns.en: I actually think it's a negative as it like the trickle down effect, not to digress too much, but you know about esports and some of the fanaticism and the youth level.
turns.zh: 我其实觉得这是件负面的事，比如那种涓滴效应（trickle-down effect）——不想扯太远——但你懂电竞以及青少年层面那种狂热。

turns.en: I don't know that it helps that side of things. The parent versus the kid who wants it more and it's for sure. It's incented the parents greatly, right?
turns.zh: 我不觉得这对那一头有什么好处。到底是家长还是孩子更想要，这个很难说，但它无疑极大地激励了家长，对吧？

turns.en: Like, hey, you can get off the payroll quick more quickly. Yeah. Yeah. We did a podcast with Scott Carl who was an MLB pitcher for a while and we're diving into all this of like just the incentives have gotten screwed up, something's got changed, it feels like.
turns.zh: 就是说，嘿，你可以更快从工资单上解脱出来。对，对。我们做过一期节目，嘉宾是在 MLB 投过一阵子球的 Scott Carl，我们深入聊过这些：激励机制已经扭曲了，有什么东西变了，就是这种感觉。

turns.en: It does. Yeah. I don't know what it takes, but I agree with that. And then like who's managing that money? Speaking of right as a wealth advisor, like you're a 18 year old getting millions of dollars.
turns.zh: 确实。是啊。我不知道要怎么办才好，但我同意这个看法。那再往下问一句：谁来管这笔钱？说到这儿，你作为财富顾问，一个 18 岁的孩子手里突然有几百万美元。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, it's like it's well documented. It's been hard enough for grown adults to manage kind of newfound wealth from so many different aspects.
turns.zh: 是啊，这已经有大量记录了。对成年人来说，管理突然到手的新财富本来就已经够难了，难点来自很多方面。

turns.en: And now it's happening to your point at a much younger age. And then the sports, especially football, right, cool, you're going to make $2 million maybe for three years, but your peers are going to make whatever, $300,000 for 40 years.
turns.zh: 而现在按你说的，这事发生在更小的年纪。再加上体育项目，尤其是橄榄球：好，你可能三年赚 200 万美元，但你的同龄人会赚——随便说个数——每年 30 万美元、赚上 40 年。

turns.en: And like the math will work out better and they have to budget themselves and all that stuff. Weird. When did you think, okay, I'm not going to the NFL, I got to think of a real job.
turns.zh: 这么一算反而更划算，而且他们还得自己做预算什么的。挺奇怪的。那你是什么时候意识到——好，我进不了 NFL，得想份正经工作了？

turns.en: Yeah. You know, I think opportunity and timing is really important. I mean, at the college football level, at any level, division one, two or three, I mean, you're with a lot of folks, they can all play, right?
turns.zh: 是啊。我觉得机会和时机真的很重要。在大学橄榄球这个层面，不管是一级、二级还是三级，你身边都是一大群能打球的人，对吧？

turns.en: And so, you know, being able to take advantage of opportunities and, you know, timing, some of those things are out of your control. I feel super blessed at the experience.
turns.zh: 所以要能抓住机会，而时机这些东西有些不在你的掌控之内。能有这段经历，我觉得自己非常幸运。

turns.en: I think it helped me just from a life experience perspective, more than anything about kind of growing up and, you know, self-advocacy and some of those types of things.
turns.zh: 我觉得它对我最大的帮助在于人生阅历层面，主要是关于成长、自我争取（self-advocacy）这类事情。

turns.en: Because when I transferred, I had to walk on off the year of eligibility and then had to re-earn a scholarship. And so, at Northwestern, at Northwestern, so that's, you know, that's, was that like Pasadena's child was playing era when, yeah, he was, I transferred there in the winter of 96 and they had just finished their citrus pole season.
turns.zh: 因为我转学的时候，得用掉那一年的资格以 walk-on（非奖学金球员）身份加入，然后重新挣回奖学金。所以是在 Northwestern——在 Northwestern，那是不是 Pat Fitzgerald 打球的那个时期？对，是他那时候。我是 96 年冬天转过去的，他们刚打完柑橘碗（Citrus Bowl）那个赛季。

turns.en: So, yeah, he had just finished Darnell Autry, I'm trying to remember all those names, but somewhere in there. Yeah. Steve Schner, Steve and I went to the same high school, Steve had a storied career at Northwestern, yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊，那批人刚打完，还有 Darnell Autry，我在努力回想那些名字，大概就是那一拨。对，Steve Schner，Steve 跟我是同一所高中的，他在 Northwestern 有过一段辉煌的球员生涯，是的。

turns.en: And then, so you got to Northwestern and you didn't convert to a Cubs fan, you stayed a Cardinals fan? I stayed a Cardinals fan, yeah. Damn it.
turns.zh: 那你到了 Northwestern 之后没有转成 Cubs 球迷，还是 Cardinals 球迷？我一直是 Cardinals 球迷，对。真该死。

turns.en: Yeah. We nearly had you. But you've had the better of that for most of the past 20 years. Well, the tide has shifted here lately, but let's hope.
turns.zh: 是啊，我们差点就把你拿下了。不过过去 20 年里大部分时间都是你们占上风。嗯，最近风向有点变了，希望继续吧。

turns.en: So, out of Northwestern, you said, hey, like every young boy's dream, I want to be a wealth advisor. What did that look like to get into that space?
turns.zh: 那么从 Northwestern 毕业后，你就跟每个小男孩的梦想一样——我想当财富顾问。要进入这个行业，当时是什么路径？

turns.en: You know, I had always been interested in markets. I think my first fascination was, you know, markets in general, and the wealth advisor path is the one that I took.
turns.zh: 我一直对市场感兴趣。我觉得我最早的痴迷就是广义的市场，而财富顾问是我走的那条路。

turns.en: You know, I needed to learn how to become a professional as opposed to a college kid. So, my first job was at Transamerica in Los Angeles. They had a two-year management training program on-campus interview at Northwestern.
turns.zh: 我得学会怎么从一个大学生变成职场人。所以我第一份工作是在 Los Angeles 的 Transamerica，他们有个两年的管理培训生项目，在 Northwestern 校园里面试。

turns.en: It was perfect, actually. I got to move to a whole bunch of different departments, mutual fund research and, you know, you name it, just to, again, learn how to be a professional and have a corporate job of sorts.
turns.zh: 其实非常合适。我轮了一大堆不同部门，共同基金研究等等，你能想到的都有，就是为了学会怎么做一个职场人、过一种公司职员式的生活。

turns.en: Were you in the famous, like, Transamerica building there in San Francisco? I was in Los Angeles. That one is San Francisco. But yeah, it was outtown LA, lived in Pasadena, went to UCLA at night to get, like, educated on the financial planning side of things.
turns.zh: 你是在 San Francisco 那栋很有名的 Transamerica 大楼吗？我在 Los Angeles，那栋楼在 San Francisco。对，是在 LA 城郊，住在 Pasadena，晚上去 UCLA 上课，补财务规划方面的知识。

turns.en: So yeah, that's where it started, the wealth advisor path. And I've always loved working with people, so that's where it started, and then spent a couple of five, six-year stints at A.G. Edwards back when it was around, great Midwest-based firm, and then Morgan Stanley for a similar period of time, which were both really good in different ways, and then joined, actually, former teammate of my net Mizzou, quarterback
turns.zh: 所以财富顾问这条路就是从那儿开始的。我一直很喜欢和人打交道，起点就在那儿。之后在 A.G. Edwards 待了两段五六年——那时候它还在，是很棒的中西部公司——然后在 Morgan Stanley 待了差不多的时间，两家各有各的好。后来我加入了我在 Mizzou 的前队友，他也是四分卫，

turns.en: as well, Kent Scornia. He founded Trilogy in 09, and I came at the beginning of 2012, and here we are. And you guys avoided any, like, quarterback, logo, or in the name, something, right?
turns.zh: 就是 Kent Skornia。他 2009 年创立了 Krilogy，我在 2012 年初加入，一直到今天。你们有没有在公司 logo 或名字里放点四分卫的元素？

turns.en: There might have been touchdown wealth advisors, contested throwing up all over a pond in our old office at one point, but our skills have diminished.
turns.zh: 也许曾经可以叫 Touchdown Wealth Advisors，我们以前办公室那儿还搞过往池塘里扔东西的投掷比赛，不过我们的技术已经退化了。

turns.en: Like, after trading here in Chicago at the trading floors at the Merc, it's right back up against the river, and cocktails were flowing, and invariably, a guy would bet some guy, like, I bet you can't throw this across the river.
turns.zh: 就像在 Chicago 的 Merc 交易大厅做交易那会儿，交易场后面就紧挨着河，酒一喝起来，总有人会跟另一个人打赌：我赌你扔不到河对岸。

turns.en: And you'd have people like, oh, sure, like $5,000, and it's probably 80 yards, right? So maybe Lamar Jackson could do it, maybe some guys could do it, but yeah, yeah, maybe.
turns.zh: 然后就有人说，哦，行啊，赌 5,000 美元，可那距离大概有 80 码吧？也许 Lamar Jackson 能扔过去，也许有几个人能，但也就是也许。

turns.en: Yeah, yeah, properly warmed up and everything, which I'm sure wasn't the case. It was not the case. And then, so always interested in markets, you were wanting to trade ever, you were like, was there ever a point like, hey, should I go hedge fund route or something?
turns.zh: 对对，还得热身充分什么的，我肯定当时完全没有。完全没有。那么，你一直对市场感兴趣，你有没有想过做交易？有没有哪一刻想过：嘿，我是不是该走对冲基金那条路？

turns.en: No, no, not necessarily. You know, more macro portfolio construction. I got my CMOS certification in those early Crilogy years to kind of align with the transition into CIO role, which was in those early days of Crilogy, and, you know, I've honestly been just blessed to have a ton of smart people around me and on our team, and we have fun doing it.
turns.zh: 没有，倒也不是。我更偏向宏观层面的组合构建。在 Krilogy 早期那几年我考下了 CIMA 认证，为的是配合我转向 CIO 角色——那也是 Krilogy 的早期阶段。说实话我一直很幸运，身边和我们团队里有大量聪明人，而且我们做得很开心。

turns.en: And what do you see, like, if you pulled out of the big shops, right, A.J. Edwards, Morgan, is that still continuing? You see, more and more, it seems to me, like, how can there be any big branch guys left?
turns.zh: 那你怎么看从大平台出来这件事——A.G. Edwards、Morgan Stanley 这种，这个趋势还在继续吗？在我看来出来的人越来越多，我都想：那些大券商分部里怎么可能还剩人？

turns.en: Because all you read about every article is like, this group pulled out and formed their own RA, this group pulled out. Yeah, interestingly, there's still so much wealth.
turns.zh: 因为你看到的每篇文章都是：这个团队出来成立了自己的 RIA，那个团队也出来了。是啊，但有意思的是，仍有大量财富留在里面。

turns.en: I mean, the predominance of wealth is still in the brick, you know, traditional investment bank firms. I mean, they have a lot of firepower.
turns.zh: 我是说，绝大部分财富还是在传统的投行系机构手里，他们火力很足。

turns.en: I think, you know, having reflected on being there prior to being in the independent space, you don't know what you don't know, really, you know, you're just used to, this is how things are, and you just don't know any different, you know, it's, again, positives on both sides of the equation, but being in the independent space, you know, for as long as I've been now and, you know, having the type of culture, it seems really cliche, but we are super intentional
turns.zh: 回想在大平台的那段经历，再对比现在做独立机构，真的是你不知道自己不知道什么，你只是习惯了事情就该这样，不知道还能有别的样子。两边当然各有好处，但在我进入独立领域这么长时间之后，我们拥有的那种文化——听起来很老套——但我们在人的问题上是非常有意识（intentional）的，

turns.en: here around our people and teammates and collaboration, and, you know, everybody's got a different experience at bigger firms, and mine certainly wasn't a bad one.
turns.zh: 无论是对团队成员还是协作。每个人在大公司的体验不一样，我自己的那段绝对不算差。

turns.en: I experienced a lot of growth and got a lot of great value from it, but, you know, the culture feel on the independent side at our firm is different.
turns.zh: 我在那里成长了很多，也收获了很大价值，但我们公司在独立这一侧的文化氛围确实不一样。

turns.en: Yeah, yeah, you still felt compelled to leave, right? Yeah. And then you mentioned, what happened to AG Edwards? They got... Yeah, they got a part by Mocopia and ultimately Wells Fargo.
turns.zh: 是啊，但你还是觉得非走不可，对吧？对。然后你提到 A.G. Edwards，它后来怎么了？他们被……对，被 Wachovia 拆掉了一部分，最后归到 Wells Fargo。

turns.en: Oh, yeah, yeah. Yeah. Yeah, so that was in the, you know, 708 period, yeah. Mocopia. I forgot about that name. Right. Was that one of those 09 bank buyouts?
turns.zh: 哦对对。是啊，那是 07、08 年那段时间。Wachovia，我都忘了这个名字了。对。那是 09 年那批银行收购案里的一个吧？

turns.en: Yeah, that's right. And then talk about, so you've got founded in 09 or you came on in 09? Kent Scornia, our founder, yeah, started the firm with like $20 million and three people, and, you know, kind of going back to the football conversation around timing and opportunity.
turns.zh: 对，没错。那说说 Krilogy——是 2009 年创立的，还是你 2009 年加入的？我们的创始人 Kent Skornia，对，2009 年创业时大概有 2,000 万美元资产、三个人，这又回到我们前面聊橄榄球时说的时机与机会。

turns.en: Kent and I remain friends, you know, post our college days and stayed in touch, and the timing just wasn't right, right out of the shoot for me.
turns.zh: Kent 和我在大学之后一直是朋友，保持着联系，但一开始时机对我来说就是不合适。

turns.en: I had literally just moved to Morgan Stanley and kind of informally partnered with a branch manager with the idea of setting up a formal team within Morgan, and again, timing was tough with GFC and management change and all those types of things.
turns.zh: 我当时刚跳到 Morgan Stanley，还跟一位分部经理非正式地搭档，想在 Morgan 内部组建一个正式团队。同样是时机不好——全球金融危机（GFC）、管理层变动等等各种情况。

turns.en: And so it was too recent for me to have just, you know, leaped from AG Edwards to Morgan Stanley and then right after it was independent. So it took a couple of years for that to happen, and, you know, we were probably managing 100 million or so in assets when I came over, and we're a little under $6 billion today.
turns.zh: 所以我刚从 A.G. Edwards 跳到 Morgan Stanley，紧接着又跳去做独立，那太快了。因此又过了几年才成行。我过来的时候我们大概管理 1 亿美元左右的资产，如今略低于 60 亿美元。

turns.en: $6 billion. And then what did that look like in 09, right? Was he purposely at that timing or just was don't like? No, I think that's just how it happened.
turns.zh: 60 亿美元。那 2009 年创业是什么样的？他是刻意选那个时点，还是就顺势而为？没有，我觉得事情就是这么发生的。

turns.en: Not a bad time to start a firm, I guess, right? When you're at the levels of the market was at and marches on 9. I have this conversation with my wife, my son was born in 09 and my daughter in 11, and we put basically the same amount of money into their college accounts, and his is like way better, right?
turns.zh: 开公司的时点也不算差吧？想想当时市场在什么位置，然后就一路上涨。我跟我太太聊过这事：我儿子 2009 年出生，女儿 2011 年出生，我们往他们的大学账户里放的钱基本一样，但儿子那个账户好得多。

turns.en: She's like, why is this so, what are you doing? Do you favor him? I'm like, no. Yeah. Like the market was at, literally he was born in February.
turns.zh: 她就问，怎么差这么多，你干了什么？你是不是偏心他？我说没有。是啊，你想市场当时在什么位置——他就正好是二月份出生的。

turns.en: Wow. And we started plowing it in right there in March at the lowest, so it's like, all right. You'll have to spread the wealth with sister at some point.
turns.zh: 哇。而我们正好从三月的最低点开始往里砸钱，所以就是这样。你以后得跟妹妹分点财富了。

turns.en: Exactly. That's a fun, I want to talk about that later, get your wealth advisor take on a college savings and whatnot. But right, like I've heard a lot of advisors before, like, oh, I was at the big bracket and I didn't like how they were handling the risk in 08, so I peeled out to start my own firm or whatnot.
turns.zh: 正是。这个话题很有意思，我想稍后再聊，听听你作为财富顾问对大学教育储蓄之类的看法。但说到这儿，我以前听过很多顾问说：哦，我当时在大平台，不喜欢他们在 08 年处理风险的方式，所以出来自己开公司什么的。

turns.en: So you did see a bit of that around that time. Yeah. Yeah, it's interesting. You know, we're thinking about, we're having those conversations on our investment team now.
turns.zh: 所以那个时期你也见到不少这样的情况。对。是啊，很有意思。我们现在投资团队内部就在讨论这些问题。

turns.en: How do you solve for left tail risk type of considerations? I mean, markets at all time highs by all accounts, things are clicking on all cylinders, earnings growth is going gangbusters, like everything seems to just be hitting right.
turns.zh: 你们怎么应对左尾风险（left-tail risk）这类考量？毕竟按各种指标市场都在历史高位，一切都在全速运转，盈利增长极其强劲，好像什么都对。

turns.en: Of course, there's plenty of noise in the background and things to be worried about. But as we know, I mean, it doesn't last forever. And so just thinking about crisis, alpha, left tail risk, uncorrelated strategies, those types of things.
turns.zh: 当然背景里也有很多噪音和值得担心的事情。但我们都清楚，这种状态不会永远持续。所以我们也在思考危机阿尔法（crisis alpha）、左尾风险、低相关策略这些东西。

turns.en: So let's dig in to all that. So where that's a newer look into that, or you guys have had some alternatives. I know you've had some stuff with us for quite a while, but yeah.
turns.zh: 那我们就来深挖一下。这是你们最近才开始关注的新方向，还是你们本来就配置了一些另类资产？我知道你们跟我们合作也有一段时间了。

turns.en: So you've had some alternatives, but you're saying, hey, this is looking more and more needed. Yeah, it's, you know, if you think about the wealth creation, it's just so above trend for so long now for most people.
turns.zh: 也就是说你们本来就有一些另类资产，但你现在觉得越来越有必要了。对，你想，如果看财富创造，对大多数人来说它已经远远高于趋势水平太久了。

turns.en: I mean, our work is always financial planning based and focused first to help kind of guide and dictate the appropriate strategy and portfolio construction.
turns.zh: 我们的工作始终以财务规划（financial planning）为基础、为先导，用来指引并决定合适的策略和组合构建。

turns.en: And, you know, everybody's had, you know, generally speaking, if seemingly you're taking some meaningful level of market risk outside, outsized returns relative to expectations.
turns.zh: 总体来说，只要你承担了相当程度的市场风险，这些年大家的回报都明显超出预期。

turns.en: It's now a lot of conversations about not only preserving, but turning into cash flow during the distribution phase of that process as they transition close to or into retirement.
turns.zh: 现在大量的讨论不只是保住这些财富，而是在他们临近或进入退休时，如何在支取阶段（distribution phase）把它变成现金流。

turns.en: So when you kind of factor all those things in together and just recognize where markets are, historical valuations, all the things you see floating around in the financial media and so forth.
turns.zh: 所以把这些因素放在一起，再认清市场目前的位置、历史性的估值，以及财经媒体上到处流传的各种说法。

turns.en: Yeah, it's more front and center for us and to make sure our advisors have the tools in the toolbox. It's ultimately, at the end of the day, we're not going to, our investment team and committee isn't going to dictate how an advisor should run their practice, but we sure as heck better equip them with all the tools and resources they need to.
turns.zh: 是啊，这件事对我们来说变得更突出了，我们要确保顾问的工具箱里有工具。说到底，我们的投资团队和委员会不会去规定某个顾问该怎么经营他的业务，但我们一定要把所需的工具和资源都给他们配齐。

turns.en: Yeah, so what does that look like? How many advisors and then they each get to pick their portfolio, you have an approved list or what does that look like?
turns.zh: 那具体是什么样？你们有多少位顾问，他们是各自挑组合吗，还是有一个核准名单？具体怎么运作？

turns.en: Yeah, we have model portfolios that we run. We hired a technical analyst about four years ago who's added tremendous value to our process that really complement the more traditional fundamental work.
turns.zh: 我们有一套自己管理的模型组合（model portfolios）。大约四年前我们雇了一位技术分析师，他为我们的流程增加了巨大价值，真正补充了更传统的基本面工作。

turns.en: We've got a quant analyst, so we have got a lot of tools in the toolkit, some of course more tactical in nature with the technical analysis piece, some more strategically based.
turns.zh: 我们还有一位量化分析师，所以工具箱里工具很多，技术分析那块偏战术性，另一些更偏战略。

turns.en: We'll use individual equities, we'll use ETS, we'll use mutual funds, all the above on the public market side of things, individual bonds, muties, et cetera.
turns.zh: 在公开市场这边，个股、ETF、共同基金我们都用，全都会用，还有个券、市政债（munis）等等。

turns.en: And then private markets, it's been an effort for us really out of the chute. I mean, the last 12, 13 years plus, I mean, private markets themselves have evolved so much just in terms of how to solve for and the different structures and asset classes that one can now get access to that they couldn't in the past, which is really exciting.
turns.zh: 然后是私募市场（private markets），从一开始就是我们努力的方向。过去十二、十三年多，私募市场本身演进得非常快——在如何解决问题、不同的结构和资产类别上，如今能接触到的东西是以前接触不到的，这非常令人兴奋。

turns.en: And so we've approved one-off solutions pretty slow and methodically over time, really just again, trying to cover all the bases or as many as we can from a resource perspective.
turns.zh: 所以这些年我们逐个核准具体方案，节奏相当慢而有条理，就是想覆盖所有可能的需求，或者在资源允许的范围内尽可能多覆盖。

turns.en: And ultimately, it's up to the advisor to continue to kind of lean in and learn to incorporate with clients or not. It's not always needed, right?
turns.zh: 最终还是要靠顾问自己持续投入、学习，再决定是否用给客户。它并不总是必需的，对吧？

turns.en: You definitely don't always need to solve with private markets or alts, but I think it's an increasing one. Not on this podcast. You always need to solve with alts on this podcast.
turns.zh: 你确实不一定每次都要用私募市场或另类投资来解决问题，但我认为这个需求在上升。在这个节目上可不是这样。在这个节目上你永远都得用另类投资来解决问题。

turns.en: That's right. That's right. Well, especially now, right? I mean, you haven't needed to be diversified in markets for a long time. If you're a large cap tech, you're fine.
turns.zh: 没错，没错。嗯，尤其是现在。这些年你其实不需要分散化，只要拿着大盘科技股，你就没事。

turns.en: And what's your personal and firm view on that of like, but I could argue this, it looked just as scary five years ago, 10 years ago, 20 years ago, right?
turns.zh: 那你个人和公司对此怎么看？我也可以这么讲：五年前、十年前、二十年前，看起来也一样吓人，对吧？

turns.en: Like it's almost always the case that we're kind of burying along and it seems irrational and it just, it's like the whole world is set up to keep this thing propped up.
turns.zh: 好像一直都是这样：我们一路闷头往前冲，看起来很不理性，感觉整个世界都被设计成要把这个东西撑住。

turns.en: And the smart ones know it can't always last, but in the meantime, the dumb people are the, or I won't say smart and dumb, but the risk blinders, blinders onto the risk are just like, what?
turns.zh: 聪明人知道这不可能永远持续，但与此同时——我不说聪明和笨——那些给风险戴上眼罩的人就是：什么风险？

turns.en: Just buy it. Just three X in video. What could go wrong? Yeah. Yeah. I mean, it's always appropriate, right? To have some level of just market beta and just be in the game, but you know, concentration wise, I'd heard the staff the other day.
turns.zh: 买就完了，直接上三倍杠杆，能出什么问题？是啊，是啊。始终保留一定程度的市场贝塔（market beta）、留在场内，这总是合适的，对吧？但说到集中度，我前几天看到一个统计数据。

turns.en: I mean, when not if open AI and anthropic end up going public, it's like the top 13 names are 50% of the, 50% of the, the S&P, I mean, so from a market cap perspective, you know, so like give or take, they're right, like really close.
turns.zh: 我是说，等到 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 上市——是等到而不是如果——那时候前 13 大成分股大概就占标普 500 的 50% 了，从市值角度看，差不多就是这样，非常接近。

turns.en: So gosh, how, how diversified can you be? I mean, you know, you debt's definitely right to be, to have some again, level of beta and inevitably you're getting the AI exposure, but you know, if you look at the private markets, some of the, you know, hedge strategies or, or, you know, trend strategies, which are less than non-correlated or, or even, you know, venture and private equity tend, tend to be again, in the right situation, really nice compliments and, and really benefiting
turns.zh: 天呐，那你还能有多分散？你说得对，保留一定贝塔肯定是对的，而且你不可避免地会拿到 AI 的敞口。但如果你看私募市场，一些对冲策略、趋势策略——它们的相关性更低甚至不相关——还有创投和私募股权，在合适的情形下往往是非常好的补充，而且能真正受益于

turns.en: from the, the US economy in a much more meaningful way. Again, it's become so funneled and narrowed on the public market side. There's so much of the economy that, that folks just are participating in when they're just in public markets alone.
turns.zh: 美国经济，且是以更有意义的方式。公开市场这一侧已经变得如此集中、如此狭窄，如果你只投公开市场，经济中有很大一部分你其实根本没有参与。

turns.en: What, what would you say, I'm a client, I'm arguing, hey, I think it is a win or take all economy of the future and there's going to only be a handful of these big tech firms that own everything, right, that drive all this AI, that have the content, that do all this.
turns.zh: 那你会怎么回应？假设我是一个客户，我在争辩说：嘿，我认为未来就是赢家通吃的经济，最后只会有屈指可数的几家大科技公司拥有一切，驱动所有 AI、掌握所有内容、做所有事情。

turns.en: So why, why do I need that long tail of those other equities? Like why do I need an index at all? An index on the public side? Yeah. Right. If, if 50% is those names, like, yeah, maybe I'm cool with it cause right, that's a winner take all scenario and I believe that's what's going to happen.
turns.zh: 那我为什么还需要其他股票那条长长的尾巴？我为什么还需要指数？公开市场这边的指数？对。是啊，如果 50% 都是那几只股票，那我可能也能接受，因为这就是赢家通吃的情景，而我相信这会发生。

turns.en: Yeah. You know, the, the challenge would be that's the belief and that belief existed in 99 and that belief existed in 2007, right? So, you know, if you have some level of exposure there is prudent, right?
turns.zh: 是啊。问题在于那是一种信念，而这种信念在 1999 年存在过，在 2007 年也存在过，对吧？所以保留一定程度的敞口是审慎的。

turns.en: But you know, the, the math certainly shows if you weather the downturns in a much more meaningful way that the compounding wealth effect and kind of smoothing out the ride, if you will, is going to help you win in the end, um, particularly too, when you, when you consider one's timeframe, right, like you may say, look, I'm looking to, I'm looking to shut things down or become fully, fully dependent on my portfolio for cash flows in
turns.zh: 但从数学上看，如果你能更有意义地熬过下跌，那种复利的财富效应、把这段路程熨平，最终会帮你胜出，尤其当你考虑自己的时间跨度时。你可能会说：看，我打算收摊了，或者我要完全依靠组合提供现金流来

turns.en: retirement. I mean, the, the market doesn't care about your timeframe, right? I mean, yeah, it's going to, it's going to be. You can't announce bad earnings cause Jeff's, Jeff's about to retire.
turns.zh: 过退休生活。可市场并不在乎你的时间跨度，对吧？是啊，它就是这样。公司不会因为 Jeff 快退休了就宣布一份糟糕的财报。

turns.en: Right. Right. Yeah. So it's, I think in periods like this, and again, I'm not suggesting that the top is even there. I just think the prudence around, um, diversifying into other markets, both public and private.
turns.zh: 对，对。是啊。所以我觉得在这样的时期——我并不是说顶部已经到了——把资金分散到其他市场（无论公开还是私募）是一种审慎。

turns.en: I mean, we have a call this afternoon with our team in regard to fixed income in the bond market. I mean, this is of course the moment, you know, when the 10 year is at 475 and you know, folks are wondering why any bonds are owned in the portfolio.
turns.zh: 今天下午我们团队要开一个关于固定收益和债券市场的电话会。这当然是那种时刻：10 年期国债收益率在 4.75%，大家开始质疑组合里为什么要持有债券。

turns.en: Exactly. They're once again, flat to negative year to date, like, why are we doing this? It's, it's, you know, that's a panic on the bond side akin to bottoming inequities.
turns.zh: 正是。它们今年以来又是持平到负收益，大家就想：我们为什么要做这个？嗯，这种债券端的恐慌，类似于股票见底时的那种恐慌。

turns.en: That doesn't mean that the 10 year can't press higher to five, five and a half percent or beyond even, but we would suggest a lot of the damage is done there, given where cash flows are on, on fixed income even.
turns.zh: 这不意味着 10 年期不能继续走高到 5%、5.5% 甚至更高，但考虑到固定收益现在的现金流水平，我们认为大部分损害已经发生了。

turns.en: So I think it remains an important piece. Would you say your model portfolios are mainly 60, 40, like, right? Like it's weird in our space, everyone's always comparing to 60, 40 and I'm also like, who's really doing 60, 40?
turns.zh: 所以我认为它仍然是重要的一块。你们的模型组合主要是 60/40 吗？我们这个圈子里很奇怪，所有人总在跟 60/40 比较，可我也会想：到底谁真的在做 60/40？

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. No. And for sure it's not just spy and ag, right? It's like, of course, maybe it approximates that, but it's significantly more dynamic than that.
turns.zh: 是啊，是啊，不是。而且肯定不只是 SPY 加 AGG，对吧？当然，也许大体上接近那个比例，但它比那要动态得多。

turns.en: Well, like, you know, I think the other thing, well, so the short answer is there are, you know, essentially five different risk buckets in each of the, kind of the model philosophies, if you will.
turns.zh: 嗯，简单回答就是：在我们每一种模型理念里，基本上有五个不同的风险桶（risk buckets）。

turns.en: And our approach again is to, we want to give advisors and ultimately clients a large degree of choice to kind of align with their belief system.
turns.zh: 我们的做法是，希望给顾问以及最终客户足够多的选择权，让组合与他们的信念体系相匹配。

turns.en: So that may be, you know, everything from purely passive, I want as low cost as I can get, you know, kind of per our conversation earlier, or I believe the benefits of both active and passive combined.
turns.zh: 所以选择范围可以是从纯被动、成本越低越好——就像我们前面聊的那样——到相信主动与被动结合的好处。

turns.en: And so some of our solutions are truly roughly a 50-50 mix of both of those. So what we deem kind of our less efficient asset classes will have some active management.
turns.zh: 我们有些方案确实大致是两者的 50-50 混合。在我们认为效率较低的资产类别里，会加入一些主动管理。

turns.en: And then it's the daily liquid alternative solutions. And you know, I've long felt that the academic theory has been terrific in that space, but really hard to implement in a consistent and compelling way.
turns.zh: 然后就是每日流动性另类（daily liquid alternatives）方案。我一直觉得这个领域的学术理论非常出色，但要持续且有说服力地落地实现其实非常难。

turns.en: And we've, you know, again, some of it's maybe better to be lucky than good. I would attribute it to our talented team, but, you know, we've had a lot of success in the daily liquid alternative solution side of it.
turns.zh: 这一块嘛，也许运气好比实力强更重要，但我更愿意归功于我们团队的才干。总之我们在每日流动性另类方案这块取得了不少成功。

turns.en: So to your question, it might look more like a 60-20-20 for many as opposed to, you know, a 60-40. And then do you feel like some people get to that 60-40 by, well, the 20 active, whatever kind of looks like an equity or it looks like a bond from a risk standpoint.
turns.zh: 所以回到你的问题，对很多人来说它看起来更像是 60-20-20，而不是 60-40。那你会不会觉得，有些人是靠把那 20% 的主动部分——不管从风险角度看它像股票还是像债券——

turns.en: So maybe we jam it into that bucket. Well, that's really critical, right, is understanding the risks that you're actually taking. So that 20%, let's call it an alt sleeve.
turns.zh: 硬塞进那个桶里，从而凑成 60-40？这一点非常关键，就是要理解你实际承担的风险。那 20%，我们就叫它另类仓位（alt sleeve）。

turns.en: I don't love the alt stigma, by the way, it has a negative connotation, but for, you know, it's, yeah, it's important. They're not certainly all created equal.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，我不喜欢「另类」这个标签，它带有负面含义。但确实重要，而且这些策略肯定不是生而平等的。

turns.en: I mean, commodities, you know, long commodities would be a high ball solution where, you know, merger arbitrage, market neutral, I mean, there's a whole bunch of different ways to play that sleeve.
turns.zh: 比如商品，做多商品会是一个高贝塔（high beta）的方案，而并购套利（merger arbitrage）、市场中性（market neutral）则是另一类，这个仓位有一大堆不同的玩法。

turns.en: It's got to, you know, it doesn't have to be non-correlated, but it sure should be quite a bit less and it should help hold up the portfolio when equities falter.
turns.zh: 它不一定要完全不相关，但相关性肯定应该低不少，而且在股票走弱时应该能撑住组合。

turns.en: Yeah. That I'd get wonky for a minute, right? Like you could even have something positively correlated, but it's negatively correlated at the right time.
turns.zh: 对。我在这儿较真一下：你甚至可以有一个正相关的东西，但它在关键时点是负相关的。

turns.en: Yeah, you bet. And yeah, which is basically managed futures can act like that, right? I mean, I'd say they're non, but for a lot of time, they're long stocks, they're long bonds, they're in the same positions.
turns.zh: 对，没错。基本上管理期货（managed futures）就可以这样表现，对吧？我会说它们是不相关的，但很多时候它们做多股票、做多债券，跟大家持仓一样。

turns.en: You bet. Yeah. It just can switch. Absolutely. Which a lot of people miss of like, it's the path of the correlation, not just the raw number over X.
turns.zh: 没错。是啊，它只是可以切换。完全同意。这一点很多人忽略了：关键是相关性的路径，而不只是某段时间的那个原始数字。

turns.en: Exactly right. Here at the time. Yeah. Well said. So, you mentioned you don't like, oh, it's what, what would you call it? Is that more from the clients?
turns.zh: 完全正确，就是在特定时间点。说得好。那你提到你不喜欢「另类」这个词，那更多是来自客户的原因吗？

turns.en: Yeah. But that's, that's what the solutions that are anything other than less than daily liquid, right? That I can't buy on the exchange basically.
turns.zh: 是啊。但那指的是所有非每日流动性的方案，对吧？基本上就是那些我不能在交易所买到的东西。

turns.en: But do you feel like clients have an aversion to that term, to the Alts term, or it just starts a whole conversation of like, what, what? It's probably my own thing.
turns.zh: 但你觉得客户是对「另类」这个词有反感，还是它会引发一整轮「什么？什么？」的对话？这可能是我自己的问题。

turns.en: Alts feel like it's, it's, it shouldn't, shouldn't be doing this kind of thing, right? Yeah, right. Like this is like way out, you know, bleeding edge of sensibility, maybe.
turns.zh: 「另类」听起来就像是——你本来不该做这种事情，对吧？是啊。就像这已经远远超出了合理边界，可能是最激进的那一档。

turns.en: Yeah. All right. I'll work on that. I don't want to, I don't want to make that any bigger than that. And then, so what is that suite of privates that you guys look at?
turns.zh: 是啊。好，我会注意这个问题，我不想把它说得比实际更严重。那么，你们关注的那一整套私募产品都有哪些？

turns.en: You mentioned a couple of there, so it's basically all hedge fund categories? You know, it could, it could be hedge funds, it could be tax favorable hedge funds, it could be infrastructure, you know, private credit or private lending in general, it could be private real estate, secondaries, it's been a really hot space for the last few years, both on the venture side and especially like late-stage growth equity.
turns.zh: 你刚才提到几类，那基本上是所有对冲基金的类别吗？可以是对冲基金，可以是税收优惠型对冲基金（tax-favorable hedge funds），可以是基础设施，可以是私募信贷（private credit）或广义的私募借贷，可以是私募房地产，可以是二级份额（secondaries）——过去几年这块非常火，无论是创投端，尤其是后期成长股权（late-stage growth equity）。

turns.en: That's like getting a piece of anthropic. Exactly. Last year or something like that. Right. Yeah, exactly right. It could be, you know, private equities, you know, a small mid-market buyout.
turns.zh: 那就像能拿到一块 Anthropic 的份额。没错，比如去年之类的。对，完全正确。也可以是私募股权，比如中小型市场的收购（small/mid-market buyout）。

turns.en: I mean, this, this sample set is just so large. I mean, to the comment earlier around truly participating in the U.S. economy and Blackstone has great educational pieces on, you know, companies that have a certain threshold of revenue higher than a hundred million in revenue in the U.S., I mean, most of them are private by a significant margin.
turns.zh: 这个样本集实在太大了。回到前面说的真正参与美国经济——Blackstone 有一些很好的科普材料，讲美国收入超过一亿美元这个门槛的公司，其中绝大多数都是私营的，而且比例高得多。

turns.en: It's like 87% or something like that. So I think that resonates with folks like, gosh, you know, if I'm in the Mag7 or I'm in the top 10 to 15 publicly traded S&P names, and I truly do really have a narrow focus here, there's so much more to the U.S. economy that I could be participating in.
turns.zh: 大概是 87% 左右。所以我觉得这会引起共鸣：天呐，如果我只持有 Mag 7，或者只持有标普前 10 到 15 大上市公司，那我的关注面确实很窄，美国经济里还有太多我可以参与的部分。

turns.en: It doesn't come without risk, of course, right? Liquidity being, you know, one of the highlights, but from a long-term perspective, you can certainly be additive.
turns.zh: 当然这不是没有风险的，流动性是其中一个重点，但从长期角度看，它确实能带来增益。

turns.en: Yeah. Isn't that, is that a little surprising to you, right? There's been so much private equity money for so long in so many deals, like you'd feel like every good private company's been snapped up, like five, 10, 20 years of that going on massively.
turns.zh: 是啊。这会不会让你有点意外？这么多私募股权资金、这么长时间、这么多交易，你会觉得每家好的私营公司早就被抢光了，毕竟这种事已经大规模持续了五年、十年、二十年。

turns.en: Yeah. It's interesting though, like if you think about, do you think about like the cloud computing, if you think about the internet, if you think about the mobile transition, if we think about all these, let's call them, you know, innovation cycles, technology cycles over time.
turns.zh: 是啊。不过很有意思，你想云计算、想互联网、想移动化转型，想所有这些——我们就叫它们创新周期、技术周期吧。

turns.en: And now, of course, we're amidst AI at whatever stage it is. I mean, there's so much incredible innovation that's happening in these new companies that are being born and just growing faster than ever, doing more with less.
turns.zh: 而现在，我们正处在 AI 之中，不管它处在哪个阶段。这些新诞生的公司里正在发生大量惊人的创新，它们增长得比以往任何时候都快，用更少的资源做更多的事。

turns.en: I think that's, it's super exciting for the U.S. economy on a go forward. So irrespective of whether we're close to the top or not close to the top, I mean, they're still, you know, the future winners, the future Meg 7s are being born in this moment.
turns.zh: 我觉得这对美国经济往后的发展非常令人兴奋。所以不管我们是不是接近顶部，未来的赢家、未来的 Mag 7 正是在此刻诞生的。

turns.en: I think that's really exciting for investors. And I've just seen friends in private equity and firms that have gotten bought, they don't just sail off into the sunset, they're going to start another company or their next level of executives or the team has like just got paid out, maybe they go sail for a couple of months or something.
turns.zh: 我也见过私募股权圈的朋友，公司被收购之后他们并不会就此扬帆退休，而是要再创办一家公司，或者他们的下一层高管、整个团队刚拿到套现，也许去 sailing 两个月什么的。

turns.en: And then they're like, all right, what's next? So I think that's where that next layer of private equity investments comes from. So yeah, those people are performers, right?
turns.zh: 然后他们就想：好，下一步做什么？所以我觉得下一层私募股权投资就是这么来的。是啊，这些人天生就是要做事的，对吧？

turns.en: They're born to build and create and are inspired by that. It's, yes, they've done well financially, I assume, over time, but it's in so many cases, it's way more than that, right?
turns.zh: 他们生来就是为了建设和创造，并被这件事激励。是的，他们在财务上应该一直很成功，但很多情况下，远不止于此，对吧？

turns.en: They've got a little bit of, is the entrepreneurial folly too, like, oh, that worked. That's easy. I bet I could do that in the next, right?
turns.zh: 这里面也有一点创业者的自负：哦，那个成了，看起来很简单，我打赌下一个我也能做，对吧？

turns.en: I can try that now over here. And a lot of times it doesn't work, but sure, yeah, that's what keeps the world moving. That's exactly right. Yep.
turns.zh: 我现在就能在这边试试。虽然很多时候并不成，但没错，正是这种劲头推动世界前进。说得太对了，是的。

turns.en: And interested on your thoughts, you thought you kind of sounded like AI is going to be this productivity push and fuel the economy even more.
turns.zh: 我想听听你的看法。你刚才听起来像是认为 AI 会成为一次生产力推动，让经济更加火热。

turns.en: My theory is we have a big risk that it causes a big recession, right? That there's, oh, I think that's right, a lot of labor costs are removed, which means people's salaries, speaking of anthropic, and I've said this on the pot a few times, I saw a deck that said they're trying to take 15 trillion of labor costs out of the market, which is basically 15 trillion of spending.
turns.zh: 我的理论是，它有很大风险引发一场大衰退，对吧？因为有——哦，我觉得这点你说得对——大量人力成本被消除，也就是人们的工资。说到 Anthropic，我在节目里讲过几次：我看到一份材料说他们试图从市场里拿掉 15 万亿美元的劳动力成本，而这基本上等于 15 万亿美元的支出。

turns.en: So I'm like, that can't be good for anybody, right, for the economy. So yeah, what are your overall thoughts there of maybe the market goes higher?
turns.zh: 所以我就想，这对任何人、对经济都不可能是好事吧。那么，你对此的总体看法是什么？也许市场还会更高？

turns.en: I think it, I think you're right. I think it's, I think our fixation has been on like the infrastructure and the large language models as it relates to AI.
turns.zh: 我觉得你说得对。我们在 AI 上的注意力一直集中在基础设施和大语言模型上。

turns.en: It's really about, I think the next phase of it, which plays out in my opinion over the next few years of the businesses that are born on a lot of that heavy lifting and spend that's taking place.
turns.zh: 我认为真正的重点在下一阶段——在我看来会在未来几年展开——也就是那些建立在当前大量重投入和支出之上的企业。

turns.en: I mean, I think you're right that it ultimately ends in a downturn and it's probably not too different from those big majors that we've discussed already.
turns.zh: 我觉得你说得对，它最终会以一场下行收场，而且大概和我们已经讨论过的那些大事件没什么不同。

turns.en: Obviously, I don't know the timing of that. I don't think it's an imminent thing though. I think that's probably a slower moving phenomenon.
turns.zh: 当然，我不知道时点。但我不认为这是迫在眉睫的事，它大概是一个演进较慢的现象。

turns.en: I mean, there's plenty of factors to go along with that, the 40 trillion and debt and significant deficits and the pressure on rates. I mean, right, there's a culmination of factors I think that come into play.
turns.zh: 还有很多因素叠加在一起：40 万亿美元的债务、巨大的财政赤字、利率压力。我认为是一系列因素共同作用的结果。

turns.en: I just think it, my sense is that because it's such a topical concern right now tells me that we're probably way early. Yeah, right. If we're all talking about it, it's not going to happen yet.
turns.zh: 我的感觉是，正因为它眼下是如此热门的话题，说明我们大概还早得很。是啊，如果人人都在讨论它，那它就还不会发生。

turns.en: Yeah, but it, to me, a lot of people are like, are you crazy? Like they're building to take away jobs and then maybe it's a weird, I don't think stagflation maybe is the right term, but like the market's at all time highs.
turns.zh: 是啊，但对我来说，很多人会说：你疯了吗？他们建设这些就是为了取代工作岗位。也许这是个奇怪的说法，我不觉得滞胀（stagflation）是正确的词，但市场在历史高位，

turns.en: But this underlying consumer economy is hollowed out and maybe for your clients and a lot of people that listen to this podcast, that's just fine.
turns.zh: 而底层消费经济却被掏空了。也许对你的客户和很多听这档节目的人来说，这完全没问题。

turns.en: They've got investments that are doing well, but it seems like that would be unsustainable for, you know, you don't have any more revenues coming in for a lot of those.
turns.zh: 他们的投资表现很好，但这看起来是不可持续的，因为很多人不再有收入进来了。

turns.en: Yeah, I guess it does make me wonder though around, you know, there's been disruptive technology forces in the past that, you know, changed kind of the job market and a lot of the professions that once existed that now don't.
turns.zh: 是啊，不过这确实让我思考：过去也有过颠覆性的技术力量，改变了就业市场，让很多曾经存在的职业消失了。

turns.en: It just does make me wonder like what, what exists in the next five, 10, 15 years from a profession perspective that doesn't exist now that we're not even thinking about, right?
turns.zh: 这让我好奇：未来五年、十年、十五年，从职业角度会出现哪些现在还不存在、我们甚至还没想到的东西？

turns.en: Somebody running, somebody responsible for managing instead of people, they're managing the agents in the, in the firm, the AI agent, I don't know, I mean, my, my ways, all that past stuff like repute, replace labor where this is like replacing the actual brain.
turns.zh: 比如有人负责管理的不再是人，而是公司里的 AI 智能体（AI agent）。我不知道，我的意思是，以往那些技术替代的是体力劳动，而这次替代的是大脑本身。

turns.en: Yeah. So it's like, you don't have to hit these buttons anymore. Now you can go over here and hit these buttons. Yeah. Um, this is like, no, we don't need your brains at all.
turns.zh: 是啊。以前的逻辑是：你不用再按这些按钮了，你可以去那边按那些按钮。而现在这个是：不，我们完全不需要你的大脑。

turns.en: Yeah. We got to figure that. Think about the value though, and, you know, in day to day interactions on pick, pick your business of, of the people skills though, right?
turns.zh: 是啊，我们得想清楚这件事。不过想想另一方面：在日常互动中，随便挑哪个行业，与人打交道的技能是有价值的，对吧？

turns.en: It's, it's what I tell my, my older two that are out of college night, you know, the, the value of, of being good with people, a good communicator, like it's, I don't think that's going away.
turns.zh: 我就是这么跟我那两个已经大学毕业的孩子说的：善于与人相处、是个好的沟通者，这种价值不会消失。

turns.en: I think that the value of that in the future is even more critical. And that's, I'm surprised there hasn't been a, where I remember the whole Robo advisor move.
turns.zh: 我认为未来这种价值甚至更加关键。说到这儿，我挺惊讶还没有出现——我还记得当年那波智能投顾（robo-advisor）浪潮。

turns.en: Yeah. Oh yeah. Whatever that was five years ago, I'm surprised there hasn't been like AI advisor moves here. Yeah. I'm like, Hey, you don't have to call your, you know, and a lot of young people don't like talking to people anyway.
turns.zh: 是啊。哦对，五年前那波东西。我惊讶的是这里还没出现「AI 顾问」这种动作。我就想：嘿，你都不用打电话给你的顾问了，而且很多年轻人本来就不喜欢跟人说话。

turns.en: So if they're on their phone and can interact with their agent. Well, I think that's coming. I feel like Robin Hood and, and maybe some of the others are, are working through that.
turns.zh: 所以只要他们在手机上和自己的智能体互动就行了。嗯，我觉得这会来的。我感觉 Robinhood 也许还有其他几家正在推进这件事。

turns.en: I don't know to the extent that it's live or actually happening, but yeah, definitely heard conversation of it. Yeah. Hopefully we'll be out of the way by then.
turns.zh: 我不知道它已经上线到什么程度、是否真的在发生，但确实听到过相关讨论。是啊，希望那时候我们已经退休让路了。

turns.en: You mentioned private equity and private credit like over the last two years where you, you know, the liquidity is the big risk there. The credit, especially with like blue owl and all those groups putting up gates and all that.
turns.zh: 你提到私募股权和私募信贷，过去两年里流动性是最大的风险。尤其是信贷这块，Blue Owl 那些机构都设了闸门（gates）。

turns.en: What's that surprising or dismaying or what was your take on that? In fairness, you know, we, we've been much more lukewarm for the past couple of years.
turns.zh: 这让你意外还是沮丧，你怎么看？说句公道话，过去几年我们对这块的态度要冷淡得多。

turns.en: I mean, ever since you see the unemployment rates, yeah, I mean it's, there's an inevitability aspect there that you can't go from zero to five in short order without having some consequence.
turns.zh: 我是说，自从你看失业率——对——这里面有一种必然性：你不可能在短时间内从 0 升到 5 而不产生后果。

turns.en: So we have certainly some solutions on the platform. We've been much more lukewarm on it for the past couple of years, but you know, outside of a few specific examples, by and large, this, the space is holding up just fine.
turns.zh: 我们平台上当然有一些相关方案，但过去两年我们对它明显更冷淡。不过除了个别案例，总体上这个领域表现得还不错。

turns.en: I mean, even, even some that are in the news, it's like, you know, you get this negative headline risk and I don't want to name names, but like yet the strategies are positive year to date.
turns.zh: 甚至一些上了新闻的案例——你会遇到这种负面的标题风险，我不想点名——但那些策略今年以来的收益其实是正的。

turns.en: And by the way, the bond market's negative. So it's, you know, there's a lot of, there is a lot of noise. I, you know, I don't want to be totally dismisses of it.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，债市是负的。所以这里面有很多噪音，我不想完全否定这些担忧。

turns.en: I mean, dismissive of it and, you know, a lot of cruels are happening and increasing. But again, I think that's just a, a function of the historic rise in rates and kind of the persistency around it as well.
turns.zh: 我不是要轻视它，确实有很多残酷的事情正在发生、并且在增加。但我认为这不过是利率历史性上升及其持续性的结果。

turns.en: And then, you know, interestingly in the real estate, like I would argue that, you know, private credit's probably going through a similar type cycle where, you know, there's this troughing phase and then, you know, you come out on the other side, there's opportunities amidst it, takes a couple of years to work through.
turns.zh: 然后有意思的是房地产：我认为私募信贷可能正在经历类似的周期，有一个筑底阶段，然后你从另一头出来，其中蕴含机会，需要几年时间来消化。

turns.en: I mean, that really happened on the real estate side for the, you know, better part of three or four years. And I feel like that pendulum is swinging in the, in the better direction, you know, even, even despite the rate pressure we've seen.
turns.zh: 房地产那边这种情况其实持续了三四年之久。我觉得这个钟摆正在朝更好的方向摆动，即便我们看到利率压力。

turns.en: And private equity, you've seen less distributions there, a little bit of a different experience than... Yeah, that's a... Yeah, for private equity and venture alike, which does make the secondary space interesting.
turns.zh: 而在私募股权这边，你看到的分配（distributions）更少，体验有点不一样……是啊，那是……对，私募股权和创投都一样，这确实让二级份额（secondaries）这块变得有意思。

turns.en: That's been of interest to us for a while. I mean, if you can kind of shorten that J-curve effect and get involved with businesses in their 4th, 5th, 6th year of existence under kind of a normal 10-year cycle, then that shortened that theoretical timeframe of seeing some DPI and the distributions and...
turns.zh: 这块我们已经关注一段时间了。如果你能缩短 J 曲线（J-curve）效应，在一个通常 10 年的周期里，在企业成立的第 4、5、6 年就参与进去，那就缩短了看到 DPI（分配倍数）和现金分配的理论时间……

turns.en: But, you know, I think, you know, for segments of private equity, you know, small, mid-market buyout, I mean, it's such a massive universe. And then if you look at the public small cap side of things and look at the lack of profitability, I mean, there's an interesting conversation there of having some attractive valuations and opportunities.
turns.zh: 但我认为，在私募股权的某些细分领域，比如中小型市场收购，那是一个极其庞大的宇宙。再看公开市场的小盘股，看看它们盈利能力有多差，这里面就有一个很有意思的话题：有相当吸引人的估值和机会。

turns.en: Obviously, it's not all created equal, but again, to the point earlier for certain clients that can be a nice compliment to the public market space.
turns.zh: 当然这些并非生而平等，但回到前面那点：对某些客户来说，它可以是公开市场投资的很好补充。

turns.en: I mean, inevitably distributions will, will increase and happen again. And so hopefully we're starting to see that a little bit. Do you ever have to convince clients to the efficacy of private equity?
turns.zh: 分配终究会重新增加、重新发生，希望我们已经开始看到一点迹象了。你需要去说服客户相信私募股权的有效性吗？

turns.en: Like, I'm thinking of... Yeah. I can't remember the stats, but it's like more and more companies aren't going public at all, right? Right. Like they're just remaining private until they're a trillion-dollar value or whatever.
turns.zh: 我在想……是啊。我记不清具体数据了，但越来越多的公司根本不上市，对吧？对。它们就一直保持私营，直到估值达到一万亿美元之类的。

turns.en: So, like, how do you access that? You got to get through one of these channels. Yeah. I think the system is changing. My sense is that if we look forward in the next five to 10 years, the mechanisms for liquidity will continue to increase in a significant way, which I think is a really good thing.
turns.zh: 那你怎么接触到这些公司？你得通过这些渠道之一。是啊，我认为整个体系在变化。我的感觉是，展望未来五到十年，流动性机制会大幅增加，我认为这是非常好的事。

turns.en: You know, I think it's for us that it's really just about education for clients. I mean, we don't want to... Obviously, we want to have a strong position and conviction around beliefs and the why and taking the long view and the benefits of incorporating certain asset classes.
turns.zh: 对我们来说，这其实只是对客户的教育问题。我们不想……显然，我们希望在这些信念上有坚定的立场和信心：为什么这样做、为什么要看长期、以及纳入某些资产类别的好处。

turns.en: But it's really an education thing. At the end of the day, there's some that we'll just say, and it's not right or wrong, we'll just say, look, I can't get comfortable with anything less than daily liquidity.
turns.zh: 但这真的是一件教育的事。说到底，有些客户就会直接说——这没有对错——他们只会说：看，凡是低于每日流动性的东西我都不舒服。

turns.en: I feel convicted there's a give-up in that for sure. And I think there's a lot of data that proves that. But if the person feels that way and sleeps best at night by not having anything that's less than daily liquid, then that's where they should be.
turns.zh: 我确信这里面肯定有收益上的让渡，也有大量数据可以证明。但如果一个人就是这么想，只有不持有任何低于每日流动性的资产才睡得最香，那他就应该待在那个位置。

turns.en: See, I can't have your job because I'd be like, why? What is it doing for you? What are you going to do with that daily liquid? Are you going to pull it all out and travel to Africa with cash on your bags?
turns.zh: 看，我就干不了你这行，因为我会问：为什么？流动性到底给了你什么？你打算拿这些每日流动性做什么？你要把钱全取出来、带着成包现金去 Africa 旅行吗？

turns.en: You're right. Yeah. Yeah. You're right. I mean, there's a careful boundary there of pushing them outside their comfort zone, right? It's more of education.
turns.zh: 你说得对。是啊，是啊，你说得对。这里面有一条需要小心把握的界线：把客户推出舒适区，对吧？这更多是教育的问题。

turns.en: Here's the why and look for consensus and buy-in as opposed to them pinching their nose and see, okay, I'll do it. And then talk to that for a second of the move.
turns.zh: 把「为什么」讲清楚，寻求共识和认同，而不是让他们捏着鼻子说：好吧，我做。那再聊一下这个转变。

turns.en: Someone came out of the big brackets and into independent advisors mainly doing ETFs. Is that the case here? What would your ETF mutual fund mix look like?
turns.zh: 有人从大平台出来做独立顾问，主要用 ETF。你们这里是这种情况吗？你们的 ETF 与共同基金的比例大概是什么样？

turns.en: No, we're pretty split. I mean, it's everything again from individual equity to ETFs to mutual funds. Yeah, I think it's definitely more passive and mutual fund.
turns.zh: 不，我们比较均衡。从个股到 ETF 再到共同基金都有。是啊，我觉得在共同基金这块确实更偏被动。

turns.en: I think nowadays too, though, you can get active management within the ETF wrapper. And we have a fair amount of that. Both really on the equity side and the fixed income side.
turns.zh: 不过现在你也可以在 ETF 的外壳里获得主动管理，我们这方面用得不少，股票端和固定收益端都是。

turns.en: And the alternative side has gotten a lot better in the ETF wrappers as well. Of course, it's not as pure and ideal in my opinion as you're going to get with a less liquid solution.
turns.zh: 另类投资在 ETF 外壳里也做得好多了。当然，在我看来它不如流动性更低的方案那样纯粹和理想。

turns.en: There's of course limitations by being able to offer daily liquidity, but that's involved I think in an effective way. And what about interval funds?
turns.zh: 能够提供每日流动性当然有其局限，但我认为这些工具用得挺有效。那间隔基金（interval funds）呢？

turns.en: Right? A little bit of both. Like, hey, you can access some of this cool private stuff. It's exchange traded, but it's not as liquid as you maybe want it to be.
turns.zh: 对吧？两种情况都有一点。就像：嘿，你能接触到一些很酷的私募资产，它可以交易，但流动性没有你希望的那么好。

turns.en: Yeah, I think those are interesting. I think to your point, I think for people to just have the peace of mind around there being a liquidity mechanism is enough.
turns.zh: 是啊，我觉得这类结构很有意思。按你说的，对很多人来讲，只要心里知道存在一个流动性机制就足够了。

turns.en: I mean, we remind people too, like if everybody's running for the exit at the same time, that's not a good time that you want to get out anyway.
turns.zh: 我们也会提醒大家：如果所有人同时冲向出口，那本来就不是你想退出的好时机。

turns.en: So the fact that a manager is going to create some liquidity restrictions there is for your benefit. As long as that's kind of message on the front end, I think that's critical.
turns.zh: 所以管理人设置一些流动性限制其实是对你有利的。只要在前面就把这个信息传达清楚，我认为这很关键。

turns.en: But that's a good point. That's probably missed by most people. And like the blue owl we mentioned stuff like, hey, they're not doing anything criminal.
turns.zh: 这话说得好，这一点大概被大多数人忽略了。就像我们提到的 Blue Owl 那类事情：嘿，他们并没有做什么违法的事。

turns.en: They're trying to protect a run on these assets. Yeah, it's protecting everybody, the entire investor base. And I think, yeah, it's easy to miss that one for folks.
turns.zh: 他们是在防止对这些资产的挤兑。对，这是在保护所有人、保护整个投资者群体。我觉得这一点大家确实容易忽略。

turns.en: But the interval fund structure I think is interesting, certainly applicable in scenarios. I mean, we have a couple of fixed income solutions that we really like.
turns.zh: 但间隔基金这个结构我觉得很有意思，在某些场景下肯定适用。我们有几只自己非常喜欢的固定收益方案。

turns.en: I mean, we've talked a little bit about, well, topically the discussions are like senior direct lending for the most part with private credit, but there's such a much more dynamic private lending, private credit space beyond that.
turns.zh: 我们聊过一点——话题上讨论私募信贷时大多集中在优先级直接放贷（senior direct lending），但在这之外，私募借贷、私募信贷的空间要动态得多。

turns.en: And I think it's a really interesting, interval funds can be an interesting way to kind of marry the benefits of public and private, for example, in one vehicle and entrust in the manager and their skill set and team and resources to have decision making around where the best opportunities are given the market environment.
turns.zh: 我觉得非常有意思的是，间隔基金可以成为把公开与私募的好处结合起来的一种方式，比如在一个工具里，把决策权交给管理人，信任他的技能、团队和资源，让他判断在当前市场环境下最好的机会在哪里。

turns.en: So I think that's an example, I think, that's interesting. I agree. Right. And like some insurance related stuff in there of lending and like that middle market that you need to term to do that deal and you can't do the term without putting it in that interval.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得这是个很有意思的例子。我同意。对。里面还有一些保险相关的放贷，以及那种 middle market 业务——你需要提供长期限融资才能做成那笔交易，而如果不放在间隔基金这种结构里，你就给不了那个期限。

turns.en: And then yeah, use that income to fund some beta, to fund some other alternatives and like that's a good looking portfolio. You bet. You bet.
turns.zh: 然后再用这些收益去配置一些贝塔、一些其他另类资产，这样的组合看起来就很不错。没错，没错。

turns.en: 351 exchanges. You guys seen a lot of that? Like is a lot of your clients wealth in these mag seven names and they want to kind of get out of it or you're not seeing that as much?
turns.zh: 351 交换（Section 351 exchange）。你们看到很多这种操作吗？是不是你们很多客户的财富都集中在 Mag 7 这几只股票上，他们想撤出来，还是说这种情况不多？

turns.en: We're not seeing a lot of it. It's definitely a topic of conversation, but we're not seeing a lot of it. We're seeing more of the long short tax solutions.
turns.zh: 我们看到的并不多。它绝对是个热门话题，但实际操作不多。我们看到更多的是多空税收方案（long-short tax solutions）。

turns.en: That's been a much more topical conversation. I mean, that's been, you know, in our experience are really effective solution. But yeah, the 351s were again, conversations are happening, but we're not seeing a lot of it.
turns.zh: 这个话题讨论得更多，按我们的经验它是非常有效的方案。是啊，351 交换也是一样：讨论在进行，但我们看到的实际操作不多。

turns.en: Yeah. That's crazy. I was reading that article a month or so ago of that AQR hedge fund that gets the money from the is now the largest hedge fund in the world, which to me is a little bit weird.
turns.zh: 是啊，太疯狂了。我大概一个月前读到那篇文章，说 AQR 那只接收 351 交换资金的对冲基金现在是全球最大的对冲基金，这在我看来有点奇怪。

turns.en: Like it cool. You're taking out of this concentrated position, you're doing some tax less harvesting, but then it's going into their hedge fund.
turns.zh: 听起来挺酷：你从集中的持仓里出来，做了些税收亏损收割（tax-loss harvesting），但钱又进了他们的对冲基金。

turns.en: Now it's locked up over there essentially, right? Like you have to pay your tax when you get it out of there. So you've changed the character and timing of it, but you still, you still have the tax over there.
turns.zh: 现在钱基本上被锁在那边了，对吧？等你从里面取出来的时候还是得交税。所以你只是改变了它的性质和时点，但那笔税还在那儿。

turns.en: Well, I think there's a couple different, you know, so that one of the AQR solutions is the is the hedge fund that has a tax piece to it. I mean, to their credit, they've had a phenomenal track record with long, short and trend kind of married together.
turns.zh: 嗯，我觉得这里有几种不同的东西。AQR 的方案之一，是那只带税收元素的对冲基金。要说他们的功劳，他们把多空和趋势结合起来，业绩记录非常出色。

turns.en: The second piece, which is more like the 351, I would suppose given that it's capital gain focused is a, is a separately managed account. So like they're able to, you know, manage the money to provide pre-tax alpha, but also defer, you know, tax, tax liability.
turns.zh: 第二块，也就是更像 351 交换的那部分——考虑到它聚焦资本利得，我猜是一个独立管理账户（separately managed account）。所以他们既能通过管理资金提供税前阿尔法，又能递延税负。

turns.en: There's no, there's no, there's never a magic bullet, right? Yeah. Completely. It's a deferral mechanism. Yeah. And then I should have mentioned this back when we're talking a little more privates and ults, but buffered notes, all that jazz, are you guys doing a lot of that or not?
turns.zh: 从来没有什么万能灵药，对吧？是啊，完全同意，它是一种递延机制。对了，我还应该在前面聊私募和另类的时候提一下：缓冲票据（buffered notes）那一类东西，你们做得多吗？

turns.en: Yeah. We've done some of it. Yeah. It's really interesting. That space, that space has gotten, yeah, massive. Really, really interesting. Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊，我们做过一些。嗯，这块真的很有意思，这个市场已经变得，对，非常庞大。真的非常有意思。

turns.en: But there's some, there's some interesting solutions there. So yeah, we've, we've done some of that. My hesitation is always like from the bank selling it to me like, why are you trying to sell me this?
turns.zh: 但里面确实有一些有意思的方案，所以我们做过一部分。我的顾虑一直是：银行向我推销这个东西的时候，我就会想——你为什么想卖给我这个？

turns.en: Right. Yeah. I instantly put up a thing of like, if you are trying to get it off your books, something feels weird. I'll circle back so my son's a senior, like, what do you tell these people if I've saved up all this money for college, I'm about to spend it down and the market's at all time highs.
turns.zh: 对，是啊。我会立刻警觉：如果你是想把它从自己的账上甩掉，那就有点不对劲。我绕回来问一下：我儿子马上高中毕业，如果你为客户攒了一大笔大学教育金、现在正要花出去，而市场又在历史高位，你会怎么跟这些人说？

turns.en: I can't do a lot of the alternative stuff I know how to do in the, in the different college savings accounts I have. So what do you tell clients of how to manage that final year of that?
turns.zh: 在我持有的那些不同的大学储蓄账户里，很多我会做的另类投资是用不了的。那你会怎么告诉客户去管理最后这一年？

turns.en: So to cash. He's a senior. Yeah. He's a senior in high school about to have a four-year college run. Exactly. Yeah. Yeah. I think with education planning, and I felt this very early in my career, early 2000s, like retirement is one thing for folks.
turns.zh: 也就是要不要转成现金。他是高中毕业班。对，他高中毕业班，接下来要读四年大学。正是。是啊。说到教育规划——我很早在职业生涯初期、2000 年代初就有体会——退休对人们来说是一回事。

turns.en: Like there's, there's various lepers you can pull, you know, you can work longer, you can live on less, like, you know, you can, you can be a little bit more flexible there at that Sarengeti hot air balloon trip.
turns.zh: 退休有很多可以拉的杠杆：你可以多工作几年，可以少花点钱，可以在那趟 Serengeti 热气球之旅上更灵活一点。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah, exactly. It's like to not have the college funds there is like from a behavioral perspective, just a different animal. Like so the short answer to the question would then be get, get more defensive and particularly because it's, it's imminent.
turns.zh: 是啊，完全正确。但如果大学资金不到位，从行为角度看完全是另一码事。所以对这个问题的简短回答就是：变得更防守一些，尤其因为这笔支出近在眼前。

turns.en: And I would expect that if it's an age-based or equity or oriented allocation that the, the growth has been outsized, probably relative to expectations for a good long run here.
turns.zh: 而且如果是按年龄下滑（age-based）或偏股票的配置，我预期这段时间的增长相对于预期来说已经超常了相当长一段时间。

turns.en: And so given that tuition is going to be due here every six months, let's call it for the next four years to dial back that risk. I don't think you need to go to, you don't need to go to the stable value fund per se.
turns.zh: 所以考虑到未来四年学费基本上每六个月就要交一次，就应该把风险调低。我不认为你需要干脆全放进稳定价值基金（stable value fund）。

turns.en: In my opinion, you know, definitely dialing back that risk allocation makes a great deal of sense. Maybe it's 20, 30, 40% equity type of thing would be my, my thought process there, given that you still do have kind of four years to fund, but exactly like, you know, if you miss this, especially what we're talking about, if it's like a blow off top, right?
turns.zh: 在我看来，把风险配置调低绝对是非常有道理的。也许股票占比降到 20%、30%、40% 这种水平，这是我的思路，毕竟你还有大约四年的时间要支付。但正是这样：如果这次你没能躲过去，尤其像我们说的那种冲顶式见顶（blow-off top），对吧？

turns.en: Yeah. Exactly. You don't want to be sitting and accelerating. Yeah. Yeah. Right. And then I've got a free tip for you when you talk to really young clients because nobody taught, right here, I'm not sure in St. Louis, but here in Chicago, like a grade school, private grade schools, 30, 40, 50 grand.
turns.zh: 是啊，完全正确，你可不想坐在那儿看着它加速下跌。对，对，没错。另外给你一个免费的建议，当你面对非常年轻的客户时——因为没人讲过这个——在这儿，我不确定 St. Louis 怎样，但在 Chicago，私立小学一年要 3 万、4 万、5 万美元。

turns.en: So I'm like, when you meet a girl in a bar, start saving, right? Like, yeah, that's right. It's known wealth management to like start saving for college when you have a baby, but no one tells you like to pay for elementary school.
turns.zh: 所以我就说，你在酒吧遇到一个女孩的时候就得开始存钱了，对吧？是啊，没错。大家都懂那种生了孩子就开始为大学存钱的财富管理建议，但没人告诉你还要为小学存钱。

turns.en: Yeah. So you meet her in the bar, start saving for elementary school. A couple less drinks. Yeah. Yeah. Costum been getting out of hand. No doubt about it.
turns.zh: 是啊，所以你在酒吧遇到她就开始为小学存钱，少喝两杯。对，对。费用确实已经失控了，毫无疑问。

turns.en: Awesome. So what, two questions, like what's, we talked a little bit about the, is that your fear or the client's fear? I kind of want to hear like what your clients and obviously they have thousands of them that have thousands of different opinions, but if you polled them, what do you think their biggest couple fears of the next year or two would be?
turns.zh: 太好了。那有两个问题：我们刚才聊的那些，究竟是你的担忧还是客户的担忧？我挺想听听你客户的想法——显然他们有几千个客户、几千种不同观点——但如果你去调查他们，你觉得未来一两年他们最大的几个担忧会是什么？

turns.en: I think this goes back to another reason why I don't think generally speaking, like this is the top of, of the market, the top of the cycle because they're, I think for the most part there is a lot of concern and fear.
turns.zh: 我觉得这又回到另一个理由，说明为什么我总体上不认为这是市场顶部、周期顶部：因为我认为大部分客户其实存在很多担忧和恐惧。

turns.en: I don't see anything close to euphoria from clients broadly speaking. They're concerned about Iran and geopolitical conflict. They're concerned about interest rates, you know, those, you know, inflation.
turns.zh: 总体来说，我在客户身上完全看不到任何接近亢奋（euphoria）的情绪。他们担心 Iran 和地缘政治冲突，担心利率、担心通胀。

turns.en: Those are the kind of the main topical things, you know, administration, whether you like the administration, whether you don't, like there's a whole litany of, I think, topical financial media type concerns, which, which is interesting because the market is at all time highs and like just based on price and based on the last handful of years of performance, you'd say, gosh, like sure feels like euphoria, but like sentiment wise, I don't, I don't
turns.zh: 这些是主要的热门话题，还有政府——不管你喜欢还是不喜欢这届政府——我觉得有一大串财经媒体式的热点担忧。这很有意思，因为市场在历史高位，单看价格、看过去几年的表现，你会说：天呐，这确实像亢奋；但从情绪上看，我不觉得。

turns.en: get there. Yeah. Vibe at all. You're not getting calls of like, hey, I want to up my AI exposure because Jim down the block just bought a new car.
turns.zh: 我完全感受不到那种氛围。你没有接到过这种电话吧：嘿，我想加大 AI 敞口，因为街角的 Jim 刚买了辆新车。

turns.en: Right. That's more characteristic of tops in my opinion, but we're not seeing that at all. And I'm involved in a lot of those conversations.
turns.zh: 对。在我看来那才是顶部的典型特征，但我们完全没有看到。而且我参与了大量这样的对话。

turns.en: Yeah. And then how do you, is that a firm mantra or each advisor of like, how do you handle the behavioral aspects? Like you mentioned the administration, you mentioned Iran.
turns.zh: 是啊。那么这是公司层面的信条，还是每位顾问各自的做法？你们怎么处理行为层面的问题？比如你提到政府、提到 Iran。

turns.en: Yeah. Like if you're invested in some of these energy stocks and the straights open, straights closed, straights open, and they're up and down 15, 20% a day.
turns.zh: 是啊。比如你持有一些能源股，然后海峡开了、关了、又开了，股价一天上下 15%、20%。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah. Right. What are those conversations like of like, hey, just stay the course, we've got a plan. Stick with the plan. Yeah. I mean, that's generally that's it.
turns.zh: 是啊，对。那种对话是什么样的？是不是就是「嘿，坚持原定路线，我们有计划，按计划来」？是啊，大体上就是这样。

turns.en: I mean, we get way more nuance than that, of course, but yeah, to be trading based on headlines of course is you have to continually be right, which is darn near impossible.
turns.zh: 当然，我们的实际讨论比这细致得多，但没错，靠新闻标题做交易，你必须一直都对，这几乎是不可能的。

turns.en: So our focus as an investment team is just really frequent communication and styles of communication with advisors that may be weekly technical analysis videos.
turns.zh: 所以我们投资团队的重点就是与顾问高频沟通、并且用多种形式沟通：可能是每周的技术分析视频。

turns.en: Maybe monthly investment meetings at a firm level. It might be an impromptu call like we have this afternoon on the bond market and how to think about it and how to frame it, how to talk to clients about it.
turns.zh: 可能是公司层面的月度投资会议，也可能是像今天下午这种临时电话会，聊债券市场、该怎么看、该怎么表述、该怎么跟客户谈。

turns.en: And maybe our weekly written, you know, memos that we do every weekend. I mean, so for us, it's just continually conversing about what we're seeing and what's important to think about both with markets and headlines.
turns.zh: 还有我们每个周末写的每周书面备忘录。对我们来说，就是持续交流我们所看到的、以及市场和新闻里哪些值得思考。

turns.en: Mainly with portfolios and changes we're making in that regard. So communication, you know, it's the old cliche, you know, good communication solves a lot of things.
turns.zh: 主要是关于组合以及我们据此做出的调整。所以沟通——这是老生常谈——好的沟通能解决很多问题。

turns.en: And that's kind of our thought process. So preempt them, right? Like get them the education, get them the answers before they ask the question.
turns.zh: 这大概就是我们的思路。所以要抢在前面，对吧？在他们提出问题之前，就把教育和答案给到他们。

turns.en: That's right. Yeah. And you started in 09, so you didn't need, you didn't have to have the big conversation there. Do we get out? Well, I started in 01.
turns.zh: 没错。是啊。而你 2009 年起步，所以你不需要经历那场大对话：我们要不要撤？嗯，我是 2001 年入行的。

turns.en: The firm started at 09. Yeah. So you had two times where you were looking at the bottom. That's right. That's right. My neighbor down the street here is a wealth advisor.
turns.zh: 公司是 2009 年成立的。是啊，所以你有两次是在看着底部的。没错，没错。我这条街那头的邻居就是位财富顾问。

turns.en: He was, I guess that was 2020. I caught up with him. He's like, I'm just a psychiatrist. Yeah. He's like, I'm not a wealth advisor. I'm a psychiatrist.
turns.zh: 我记得那是 2020 年。我跟他聊了聊，他说：我就是个精神科医生。是啊，他说：我不是财富顾问，我是精神科医生。

turns.en: I have 30 minute slots where I talk through everybody's problems and then onto the next day. Yeah. Which is that you like that part of the job or like gets tiring?
turns.zh: 我有一个个 30 分钟的时段，把每个人的问题聊一遍，然后接着下一个。是啊。那你是喜欢工作里的这一部分，还是会觉得很累？

turns.en: No, I like it. I like the human side of it. I like, I got into this business because I like working with people and I like, I guess similar to the quarterback and I like the responsibility and being accountable.
turns.zh: 不，我喜欢。我喜欢它有人情味的一面。我入这一行就是因为喜欢和人打交道，而且——大概跟四分卫类似——我喜欢那种责任和担当。

turns.en: That part's fun. I never thought of that. Like the CIO is kind of the quarterback or maybe the offensive coordinator, right? And defensive coordinator.
turns.zh: 这部分很有意思。我从来没这么想过：CIO 有点像四分卫，或者进攻协调员（offensive coordinator），对吧？还有防守协调员。

turns.en: The head coach. Yeah. Okay. We need this on the field. Yeah. The fun part is you can have offense and defense on the field at the same time.
turns.zh: 主教练。是啊，好，我们得把这套用到场上。有意思的是，你可以让进攻组和防守组同时在场。

turns.en: That's true. You're right. It should. Right. A lot of people forget that. They're like, no, it's right. Is that the old advisor model? Like, oh, we're now, we've seen the macro and we're now tilting defensive and it's like, it's more of a like, put this unit on and off, shift the, shift the allocations instead of like, this isn't always on allocation that protect things.
turns.zh: 说得对，你说得对，本来就该这样。很多人忘了这一点。这是不是旧的顾问模式？就像：哦，我们看到了宏观情况，现在要转向防守。其实更像是把某个单元换上场、换下场，调整配置比例，而不是靠一个永远开着来保护你的配置。

turns.en: That's right. Yeah. Because as we've seen risk happens fast and every day that goes by, it seems like that, you know, with algorithmic trading and, you know, I think there's just, it's going to market this move faster and faster as time goes, you know, we'll be 24 seven at some point.
turns.zh: 没错。是啊，因为我们已经看到风险来得很快，而且随着算法交易之类的发展，市场似乎每天都在变得波动更快，随着时间的推移迟早会变成 24 小时 7 天不停。

turns.en: So, for sure it's coming perpetual CMEs doing a bunch of stuff on that of like, yeah, all the prediction markets screwed up. Yeah. Speaking of it, like you have clients asking you if they should get involved in that stuff.
turns.zh: 所以「永续交易」肯定会来，CME 在这方面做了一堆东西。是啊，还有所有那些预测市场（prediction markets），全都乱套了。说到这个，有客户问过你他们该不该参与这些东西吗？

turns.en: Fortunately, no, at least that's not coming to me. I'm sure it's being asked, but and they just say, easy, no, I mean, that's like, you know, if you want to throw it, like it seems there could be some use case.
turns.zh: 幸好没有，至少没有人来问我这个。我相信肯定有人在问，但答案很简单：不。我是说，如果你想玩一把，它似乎也可能有某种使用场景。

turns.en: Sure. Right. If you knew your portfolio is going to get screwed if, if the, whatever, whoever wins the midterms or something, which in and of itself, that statement is silly, right?
turns.zh: 当然。对。如果你确定自己的组合会因为中期选举谁赢而遭殃——这个说法本身就很荒谬，对吧？

turns.en: Right. You never really know. But assuming something like that and you could hedge a little, um, yeah, who knows. Yeah. For certain things, there could be definite benefits of it, but I mostly agree.
turns.zh: 对，你其实永远不知道。但假设有这样的情况，你能做一点对冲，嗯，那就难说了。是啊，对某些事情来说它确实可能有明确的好处，但我大体同意你的看法。

turns.en: It's a, it's like, I think the stats came out like 96% of people lose money. Wow. Yeah. Messing with it. I didn't prep you for this, but we'll leave with your Mount Rushmore of football movies.
turns.zh: 就像我看到的统计，96% 的人在里面亏钱。哇。是啊，玩这些东西就是亏。我没提前给你准备这个问题，但最后我们来聊聊你心目中的橄榄球电影 Mount Rushmore（前四名）。

turns.en: Oh, so you're, you're top four. I never say your favorite cause that gets hard. Like I borrowed from Bill Simmons asking you for your Mount Rushmore.
turns.zh: 哦，就是你的前四名。我从来不问你最喜欢哪部，因为那太难选了。我这是学 Bill Simmons，问你的 Mount Rushmore。

turns.en: Wow. That's good. I'll give you, you want a list? Good. Goodness. Yeah. I mean, I, you know, the first thing that came to mind candidly was Rudy.
turns.zh: 哇，这个问题好。我给你……你要一份清单吗？天呐。是啊，说实话，我脑子里第一个冒出来的是 Rudy。

turns.en: Yeah. I was going to say Rudy. Yeah. What else do you have for me? I would go any given Sunday. Yeah. That's up there. It's the longest yard, original.
turns.zh: 是啊，我本来也要说 Rudy。还有什么？我会选 Any Given Sunday。对，那部排得上号。还有原版 The Longest Yard。

turns.en: Yeah. Bert Reynolds. I would say any given Sundays up there, Rudy's up there. You know, I think this is a little bit off topic of the question, somewhat related.
turns.zh: 对，Burt Reynolds 那部。我会说 Any Given Sunday 排得上，Rudy 也排得上。不过我觉得下面这个有点跑题，但多少相关。

turns.en: The Bo Jackson 30 for 30 is one of my favorites. He was my childhood star. I had a poster of him on the, when I was a kid, it had him and his Royals baseball uniform on one side and then his Raiders uniform running the football on the other side.
turns.zh: Bo Jackson 那部 30 for 30 是我最喜欢的之一。他是我童年的偶像。小时候我房间里有一张他的海报，一边是他穿着 Royals 棒球服，另一边是他穿着 Raiders 球衣抱着橄榄球冲跑。

turns.en: Yeah. He's a- Love it. My, my daughter is on the travel softball team out by O'Hare and it's at the Bo Dome. Oh really? New this year. I've been going there for like weeks and she's like, what's this, why is it called the Bo Dome?
turns.zh: 是啊，他真是——太喜欢了。我女儿在 O'Hare 附近的一支巡回垒球队，场地就在 Bo Dome。真的吗？今年新去的。我去了好几周，她问：这是什么，为什么叫 Bo Dome？

turns.en: Yeah. And I started explaining all this and like inside is all these quotes and like, wow. I'm like, this guy was unbelievable. Like he was the best you could be at two sports at the same time.
turns.zh: 是啊，我就开始给她讲这些，里面还挂着各种名言，我就想：哇，这个人太不可思议了，他能同时在两项运动里都做到最好。

turns.en: That 30 for 30 is a good one if you haven't seen it. All right. I'm going to put her on that. All right. I think we'll leave it there. We'll put Crilogy down in the show notes for everyone.
turns.zh: 如果你没看过那部 30 for 30，很值得一看。好，我会带她去看。好，我觉得今天就聊到这儿。我们会在节目备注里放上 Krilogy 的信息给大家。

turns.en: Take a look, give them a call, see what they're up to. And then we'll come see you next time we're in St. Louis. Please do. Thanks, Jeff. I enjoyed it.
turns.zh: 大家可以去看看，联系他们，了解他们在做什么。下次我们去 St. Louis 的时候去找你。一定。谢谢，Jeff，我很享受这次对谈。
